name: live_max_over_no_matching_rows_is_null
description: MAX over an empty set returns NULL even though the aggregated column is NOT NULL; a live engine demonstrates the NULL rather than the fixture asserting it in the abstract
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
CREATE TABLE orders (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), total NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
query_sql:
-- @name GetMaxOrderTotal
-- @returns :many
SELECT MAX(total) AS max_total FROM orders ORDER BY max_total

columns.name: max_total
columns.note: MAX returns NULL over an empty set even though total is NOT NULL

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc marks MAX(total) non-nullable because total is NOT NULL in the schema, which is wrong for an empty set
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe marks any bare aggregate nullable, and the first run here has no orders at all, so the engine actually returns the NULL

default: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.com')
INSERT INTO orders (id, user_id, total) VALUES (1, 1, 42.50)
